title: EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogue on Connectivity and Inclusion – November 2024
executive_summary: The EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogue on Connectivity and Inclusion, held in Santiago de Chile in November 2024, gathered over 35 countries from Latin America, the Caribbean, and the EU to discuss digital transformation, AI, and connectivity. Co-hosted by the European Commission, Chile, and ECLAC, the event focused on enhancing digital cooperation through secure, resilient, and inclusive connectivity, infrastructure investments, and cross-border collaboration. Key outcomes included launching the EU-LAC Female Digital Policy-Makers Network to promote gender equality in digital policy and advancing initiatives under the EU Global Gateway investment agenda. The dialogue emphasized human-centric AI governance, data protection, and leveraging high-speed infrastructure like the BELLA II submarine cable to boost research, education, and eTrade. These efforts align with the Digital Agenda for LAC and prepare for the EU-CELAC Summit 2025, aiming to foster socio-economic growth, digital inclusion, and sustainable development across both regions.
characteristics: The EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogue on Connectivity and Inclusion (Nov 5-6, 2024, Santiago) gathered 35+ countries from Latin America, the Caribbean, and the EU to discuss digital transformation, AI, connectivity, and inclusion.
Key focus areas included secure, resilient, and meaningful connectivity, infrastructure investments, cross-border connectivity, and gender equality in digital policy.
The event launched the EU-LAC Female Digital Policy-Makers Network to promote women's leadership in digital policy formulation.
The dialogue emphasized public-private partnerships, last-mile connectivity, and inclusive digital transformation for rural and remote communities.
The EU's Global Gateway supports large-scale digital projects like the BELLA II submarine cable, enhancing high-speed data transfer and regional connectivity.
Cooperation on AI governance, HPC infrastructure, and regulatory frameworks aims for human-centric AI protecting rights and fostering innovation in both regions.

Political Actors: Vice Minister of Information and Communication Technologies of Ecuador
Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
Research and Innovation Actors: Spanish Agency for the Supervision of AI
Brazil’s National Laboratory for Scientific Computing

practical_applications: Launch of the EU-LAC Female Digital Policy-Makers Network to strengthen women’s leadership and representation in digital policy formulation, promoting gender equality in the digital realm.

Deployment of large-scale digital projects under the EU Global Gateway Investment Agenda with Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) to support digital transformation aligned with shared values and interests.

Operation and expansion of the BELLA II high-speed submarine fibre-optic cable connecting the EU and LAC countries, providing faster, secure, and trustworthy data transfers to support scientific research, education, and eTrade.

EU support and engagement in legislative processes on Artificial Intelligence (AI) in LAC countries, including outreach to the Brazilian Senate on AI regulation and the establishment of the “EU-Brazil digital industry sounding board” for policy exchange.

Bilateral cooperation on High Performance Computing (HPC), exemplified by the Memorandum of Understanding between the Spanish Supercomputing Center and Brazil’s National Laboratory for Scientific Computing.
Organization of technical workshops on AI and data governance focusing on Large Language Models and linguistic diversity, including indigenous languages, within the EU-LAC Digital Alliance framework.
Regular exchange visits between LAC public institutions and European AI agencies and supercomputing centers to share best practices on algorithmic transparency, research, and innovation.

Co-funding and facilitation of the EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogues on Connectivity & Inclusion and Artificial Intelligence by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

Formulation of actionable conclusions from the EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogue on Connectivity & Inclusion focusing on cross-border connectivity, secure and resilient connectivity, infrastructure investments, and meaningful connectivity ahead of the EU-CELAC Summit 2025.
commitments: The EU aims to mobilise up to €300 billion in public and private investments from 2021 to 2027 under the Global Gateway strategy.
The BELLA II submarine fibre-optic cable has connected 65 million people so far and plans to expand to Peru, Costa Rica, Guatemala, El Salvador, and Honduras.
The EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogues held in 2024 concluded with a set of concrete initiatives to be deployed in 2025.

The EU-LAC Digital Alliance focuses on four key connectivity cooperation areas ahead of the EU-CELAC Summit in 2025: cross-border connectivity, secure and resilient connectivity, infrastructure investments, and meaningful connectivity.

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is the central political actor driving the EU-LAC Digital Alliance, providing strategic frameworks such as the Global Gateway, the EU AI Act, and coordinating with Member States and partner countries. It is prominently mentioned as a key initiator, funder, and policy leader in digital transformation, AI governance, connectivity, and cooperation with Latin America and the Caribbean.

top_actors.name: EU-LAC Digital Alliance
top_actors.justification: The EU-LAC Digital Alliance is the main platform and framework for bi-regional cooperation on digital transformation, connectivity, AI, and inclusion. It organizes the policy dialogues, fosters collaboration, and drives concrete initiatives, making it a pivotal actor in the document's context and thematic focus.

top_actors.name: Government of Chile
top_actors.justification: As co-host of the Digital Week and the EU-LAC Digital Alliance Policy Dialogue on Connectivity and Inclusion, the Government of Chile plays a key role in facilitating the dialogue and regional cooperation. Its involvement anchors the event locally and supports the implementation of regional digital agendas.

top_themes.name: Digital Infrastructure
top_themes.justification: Digital infrastructure, including connectivity, cross-border fiber optic cables like BELLA II, 5G spectrum, and investments in secure and resilient networks, is central to the document. It forms the backbone of the digital transformation efforts discussed and is critical for enabling all other digital initiatives, including AI and inclusion.

top_themes.name: Artificial Intelligence
top_themes.justification: AI is a major focus of the dialogues, with extensive discussion on governance, regulatory frameworks, human-centric AI, and cooperation between EU and LAC countries. It is strategically important for socio-economic growth and innovation, and closely linked to digital policy and data governance.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: Digital inclusion is emphasized as a key objective to ensure that digital transformation benefits all citizens, including marginalized groups such as women and rural communities. The launch of the EU-LAC Female Digital Policy-Makers Network highlights the commitment to gender equality and inclusive digital policies.
